content: The selection of appropriate footwear, as recommended by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), includes the use of therapeutic footwear such as custom-made orthotic shoes. These specialized shoes are designed to help reduce plantar pressure and prevent the development of foot ulcers. It is advised to avoid wearing open-toed shoes, as they may increase the risk of injury or complications. Additionally, footwear with specific features, such as rocker soles or metatarsal accommodations, can effectively reduce pressure on targeted areas of the foot, thereby providing enhanced protection and support.
